set.approach: Cross Taboose Pass to the John Muir Trail, then go north on it to the crossing of the South Fork of the Kings River. Shortly past the crossing a use trail heads southwest toward Cartridge Pass. Follow its faint tread past some lakes and over the low point between Cirque Crest and Mt. Ruskin, then down past the lakes until the Hershey's Kiss face appears; there are good campsites along the lakes. Tin Fish follows the obvious line left of center on the main face.
set.descent_text: Scramble northwest down sandy ledges. One choice is the long hike down and around to the base; the other is to scramble across to the large ledge belay above the roof pitch of Vibe Vendetta and rappel that route.

review.notes: Route page states scramble down and rappel option; rope count left out.

set.approach: Cross Taboose Pass to the John Muir Trail, then go north on it to the crossing of the South Fork of the Kings River. Shortly past the crossing a use trail heads southwest toward Cartridge Pass. Follow its faint tread past some lakes and over the low point between Cirque Crest and Mt. Wonka's Way goes up the left portion of the main steep face, immediately right of the broken lower-angle gullies, and starts on low-angle slabs below a large left-facing corner.

review.notes: Route + area; the rappels stated cover the lower pitches only, not the descent from the top.

set.approach: Starting in the Lakes Basin, cross the ridge and descend the gully; the wall towers on the gully's east side. Swish Dike climbs straight toward the face's high point, which lies left of center.

Park at the Lake George lot and take the Crystal Lake trail; at the Crystal Lake sign, turn left and descend to the lake. Walk around the lake, and a little farther on, a climbers trail branches left to the foot of the cliff. Highlands Wall is the first cliff reached, a northeast-facing wall visible from the parking lot.

review.notes: Area pages; route page has no text.

set.approach: Park at the Lake George lot and take the Crystal Lake trail; at the Crystal Lake sign, turn left and descend to the lake. Walk around the lake, and a little farther on, a climbers trail branches left to the foot of the cliff. Highlands Wall is the first cliff reached, a northeast-facing wall visible from the parking lot. The route begins in the large chimney at the far left end of the wall, with the bolted crystal-dike route You Only Live Twice on its left and No Time To Die on its right.

review.notes: Area + route; top-out descent not stated.

set.approach: Park at the Lake George lot and take the Crystal Lake trail; at the Crystal Lake sign, turn left and descend to the lake. Walk around the lake, and a little farther on, a climbers trail branches left to the foot of the cliff. Highlands Wall is the first cliff reached, a northeast-facing wall visible from the parking lot. You Only Live Twice follows a bolted crystal dike just left of the large chimney at the wall's far left end.
The route is on the right side of the wall in the Hinterland and climbs through some of the larger roofs.

Go up the Hinterland Gully. Before scrambling up to the large ledge below the route Autopia, start in a recess off the left-hand gully. The climb works up short dihedrals to the main ledge and finishes at the anchor shared with Autopia.
Go high up the Hinterland Gully to the south side of its left flank; the climb starts in a left-facing corner, at the same start as Ridgeback.
set.descent_text: From the bushy ledge at the top of the second pitch, head west along the ledge to trees under Ridgeback, then rappel off those trees into a loose gully.

set.approach: The route starts in the middle of the wall at the Hinterland and follows a line of weakness through the overlapping exfoliation slabs, angling slightly right to halfway and then going straight up.
Climb the Hinterland Gully as far as the foot of Crest of the Far East, then follow the base of the formation south to its left side, where the route begins on slabs.
The route is on the far left side of Hinterland Wall and begins in a left-facing dihedral.
set.descent_text: The top anchor has rappel hangers that are not suitable for lowering, so rappel only. For a rappel of just the first pitch, use the anchor left of the trees.

set.approach: The route is on Hinterland Wall and shares its first-pitch dihedral start with the route Aquarium, at the far left side of the wall.

From the Tahquitz north gully trail, a mostly level trail splits south toward the Diamondback routes. At the Diamondback buttress, go uphill west for several hundred feet to a group of large pines; Hondo Buttress faces north, just west of Diamondback's descent. Free starts by a big pine where a gully begins; a granite block there makes a comfy seat. Scramble up that gully to where the rock gets steeper.

From the Tahquitz north gully trail, a mostly level trail splits south toward the Diamondback routes. At the Diamondback buttress, go uphill west for several hundred feet to a group of large pines; Hondo Buttress faces north, just west of Diamondback's descent. Hondo Hedral climbs the visor that arches left, beside a big pine.

From the Tahquitz north gully trail, a mostly level trail splits south toward the Diamondback routes. At the Diamondback buttress, go uphill west for several hundred feet to a group of large pines; Hondo Buttress faces north, just west of Diamondback's descent. Rider starts in the gap between the pines and goes up a ramp to the smaller of two laybacks.

Hike to Iceberg Lake in the cirque above Whitney Portal, go around the lake, and work up the loose slope to the cliff bands, which sit to the north and northeast of the lake. The route starts in a large notch in the middle of the boulder pile.

Hike to Iceberg Lake in the cirque above Whitney Portal, go around the lake, and work up the loose slope to the cliff bands, which sit to the north and northeast of the lake. The route is on the tower just right of center on the western crag, which is the left-hand crag as seen from camp.
set.descent_text: Rappel the tower from a sling on a horn at the summit. Traversing the ridge east or west to descend looks possible but complicated.

set.approach: Hike to Iceberg Lake in the cirque above Whitney Portal, go around the lake, and work up the loose slope to the cliff bands, which sit to the north and northeast of the lake. The route is on the ragged cliff band along the lake's northeast side; skirt the lake's east shore and climb the scree below to the foot of the route.
set.descent_text: A rappel from the notch at the top reaches the ground.

set.approach: Hike to Iceberg Lake in the cirque above Whitney Portal, go around the lake, and work up the loose slope to the cliff bands, which sit to the north and northeast of the lake. Look for a big chimney shaped like the letter A at the right end of the lower cliff; the route enters it from the bottom and follows the crack system above all the way to the summit.

Follow the north talus approach to Tahquitz's north face and the North Gully descent, then continue much farther. The Indian Buttress formation lies just beyond the Hinterland cirque, deep in the cirque known as the Others.

review.notes: Area page only; route page is empty.

set.approach: Starting in Miter Basin, ascend the drainage below Iridescent Lake over gentle slabs and grassy meadows. At the outlet, skirt the east shore, get past a short third-class step, and take ledges up to the wall. Buns Of Steel breaches the headwall of the main tower.
set.descent_text: Either rappel the neighbouring route Civilized or walk off.

set.approach: Starting in Miter Basin, ascend the drainage below Iridescent Lake over gentle slabs and grassy meadows. At the outlet, skirt the east shore, get past a short third-class step, and take ledges up to the wall. Civilized starts at a V-shaped crack in the middle of the white tower.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route. All the anchors are two-bolt stations with links.

set.approach: Starting in Miter Basin, ascend the drainage below Iridescent Lake over gentle slabs and grassy meadows. At the outlet, skirt the east shore, get past a short third-class step, and take ledges up to the wall. The route lies at the right of the white triangular pillar that makes up the wall's left portion. Two chimney features sit at the base; the first pitch starts up the side of the right-hand chimney.
set.descent_text: To rappel the route, stop at the final bolted anchor, at the right edge of the pillar's top. The headwall above adds a short stretch to the true top.

set.approach: Approach as for the Rock Craft formation, then take a faint path heading down and east to the White Fang formation. The crack is on the south face, at the rock's lower side toward the hill.
